summary: hir_unicode_class ignored the != operator by consulting only the negated field, which tracks the \p versus \P sigil. Consequently, \p{gc!=Separator} matched separators instead of their complement, and \P{gc!=separator} incorrectly matched the complement. Calling is_negated() combines both sources of negation correctly. The fix adds a detecting assertion to class_unicode_gencat, enabled by the default unicode-gencat feature. This is a proposed reversal; no tests were run.
